title: Model Rules of Professional Conduct r. 5.4 — Professional Independence of a Lawyer
author: American Bar Association

dom.t: AI supervision: Retained responsibility is not strict liability

st.t: AI supervision: Retained responsibility is not strict liability
st.an: The source supports the cluster’s distinction between delegating legal work and permitting nonlawyer ownership or control. Rule 5.4 restricts nonlawyer ownership and leadership while independently protecting lawyers’ professional judgment; it does not address Arizona’s alternative ABS framework or establish comparative effectiveness.
qs: (c) A lawyer shall not permit a person who recommends, employs, or pays the lawyer to render legal services for another to direct or regulate the lawyer's professional judgment in rendering such legal services.

kp.d: Rule 5.4(a) prohibits lawyers and law firms from sharing legal fees with nonlawyers, subject to specified exceptions involving post-death payments, practice purchases, employee compensation or retirement plans, and certain court-awarded fees shared with nonprofit organizations.
qs: shall not share legal fees with a nonlawyer
may include nonlawyer employees in a compensation or retirement plan

kp.d: Rule 5.4(b) prohibits a lawyer from forming a partnership with a nonlawyer when any partnership activity consists of practising law.
qs: shall not form a partnership with a nonlawyer

kp.k: Third parties cannot regulate professional judgment
kp.d: Rule 5.4(c) protects lawyers’ professional independence by prohibiting a person who recommends, employs, or pays a lawyer for another’s legal services from directing or regulating the lawyer’s professional judgment.
qs: direct or regulate the lawyer's professional judgment

kp.d: Rule 5.4(d) bars practice through a for-profit professional entity when a nonlawyer owns an interest, except for temporary fiduciary estate holdings during administration.
qs: a nonlawyer owns any interest therein

kp.k: Nonlawyer governance and control are prohibited
kp.d: Rule 5.4(d) also prohibits nonlawyers from serving as corporate directors, officers, or equivalent responsible persons, and from holding rights to direct or control a lawyer’s professional judgment.
qs: a nonlawyer is a corporate director or officer
direct or control the professional judgment of a lawyer
